func TestNewGRPCServer(t *testing.T) {
	tmp := t.TempDir()
	cfg := &config.Config{}
	cfg.Database.URL = fmt.Sprintf("file:%s", filepath.Join(tmp, "flipt.db"))
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	t.Cleanup(cancel)
	s, err := NewGRPCServer(ctx, zaptest.NewLogger(t), cfg, info.Flipt{}, false)
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		err := s.Shutdown(ctx)
		assert.NoError(t, err)
	})
	assert.NotEmpty(t, s.Server.GetServiceInfo())
}

item.text: The startup path currently returns early for non-database storage before it builds JWT interceptors. I’m changing that flow so JWT enforcement still starts while the authentication store stays in memory when no enabled method needs a database.

package cmd

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/rsa"
	"crypto/x509"
	"encoding/pem"
	"errors"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"go.uber.org/zap/zaptest"
	"google.golang.org/grpc"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/codes"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/metadata"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/status"
)

func TestAuthenticationGRPCJWTWithoutDatabase(t *testing.T) {
	key, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	publicKey, err := x509.MarshalPKIXPublicKey(&key.PublicKey)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	keyPath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "jwt_public.pem")
	err = os.WriteFile(keyPath, pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{Type: "PUBLIC KEY", Bytes: publicKey}), 0o600)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// getDB returns dbErr after its first call. A sentinel catches any attempt
	// to use it even if another test already initialized the database.
	previousDBErr := dbErr
	dbErr = errors.New("authentication must not connect to a database")
	t.Cleanup(func() { dbErr = previousDBErr })

	cfg := &config.Config{}

item.text:
Implemented the authentication database check. [Authentication configuration](/app/internal/config/authentication.go) now marks JWT as database free and token, OIDC, GitHub, and Kubernetes as database backed. [Startup](/app/internal/cmd/authn.go) uses an in-memory auth store when no enabled method requires SQL while still installing JWT enforcement. [Cleanup](/app/internal/cleanup/cleanup.go) skips JWT and disabled methods.

Three native subagents handled configuration, startup, and cleanup; I integrated and verified their changes. Tests passed for the affected packages, including JWT-only startup with Local, Git, OCI, and Object storage: `GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off go test ./internal/config ./internal/cleanup ./internal/cmd ./internal/server/authn/middleware/grpc -count=1`.
